name: ANSI inhibit gate (AND with one negated input)
summary: AND outline with a bubble on one input, so that input blocks the output whenever it is active.
description: An inhibit gate passes one signal only while a second, inhibiting signal is inactive. In distinctive-shape form it is drawn as an AND outline with a bubble on the inhibiting input. It is a very common pattern in interlock logic, where a command is allowed unless a blocking condition is present.

On drawings the inhibiting input should be named for the condition that blocks, such as trip active or door open, so that the bubble reads naturally. Where the physical implementation is an AND gate fed by an inverter, the schematic may still use this compact form for clarity.
The symbol does not specify which input has priority in timing. If the inhibiting signal must arrive before the command, a sequencing note or timing element is required.
readingNotes: Identify which input carries the bubble; that input blocks the output.
Check whether the implementation includes a separate inverter.
drawingChecklist: Name the inhibiting input for the blocking condition.
Place the bubble on the correct input lead.
Note any timing priority between command and inhibit.
distinction: A NAND has its bubble at the output; an inhibit gate has its bubble on one input only.
